main_text.p: vertit. Idque ob Amasiæ deliĉtum acci-disse traditur.2.Par.25. lipas.[?] Siquidem Idumæorum fi-nes victor ingressus, idola gentis ejus asfumpserat. Hic * novem annos regnasse{a}a viginti novem[?] scribitur, quantum in libris Regnorum re-peri. Sed in Paralipomenis, atque etiam in Chronicis, novem & viginti annos imperium tenuisse annotatū *est.* abest ab ed. Col. Ea nimirum id persuadente ratione, quæ in his Regnorum libris facile perspici poterat. Ioram enim rex decem tribuum {b}octavo anno imperii Amasiæ traditur regnare cœpisse, unumq;[?] & quadraginta annos imperium tenuisse, regnante demum Ozia Amasiæ filio, quarto imperii ejus anno defunctus est.quinto decimo. Qua ratione{c}viginti & novem annos regi Amasiæ effecit.Vide Sig. Itaque nos hoc ipsum secuti, quia rationem temporum persequi placet, Chronicorum authoritati accessimus. Igitur Amasiæ, Ozia filius successit, nam in parte decem tribuum Ioas diem functus, Ioram filio locum fecerat:2.Par.26. Ozias rex, qui & Azarias.[?] postea[?] hunc Zacharias ejus filius regnavit. Horum nos regum, omniumque qui in parte decem tribuum Samariæ præ-fuerunt, annotanda esse tempora non putavimus:4.Reg.15. quia brevitati studentes, superflua

page.notes: Marginal note marks and superscript letters are small and partly unclear: the note after "lipas" and the note "2.Par.25" are read with [?]. The printed asterisks in "Hic * novem" and "annotatū *est" are kept as printed; the note "* abest ab ed. Col." belongs to the second asterisk. The note "a viginti novem" is partly illegible. The note under "b" may continue with "Vide Sig.", which is read as belonging to note c. The word "unumq;" is read with [?]. "postea" is read with [?] (the scan is faint). The note "2.Par.26 ... Azarias" is partly unclear. The long s is printed as f in some words ("deliĉtum", "asfumpserat") and is transcribed as s where it is clearly a long s. The catchword "omisi-" is the broken word at the foot of the text.
